title: New Day

location.name: The New Temple at Chapel Shore (Inner Harbor)
location.kind: harbor-shore temple site: ruins of the decaying chapel rebuilt as a futuristic white temple
location.real_analog: Oslo Opera House roof at dawn (white stone sloping into the harbor) for the temple; Baltimore Inner Harbor shoreline with wooded hills behind for the setting
near: the open sea in the distance

situation: At first light the POET rides back to the shore where the chapel decayed in poem 3 and its remnants lie in the sun. He begins to rebuild; the temple builds itself with him, not old but futuristic, modern, clean and white. He is alone. The interior beats (choir chords, journal, gospels sung to a mirror) are inferred staging for a poem the treatment marks '[poem unwritten]'.
weather_light: chilly morning; low sun revealing the ruins; mist on the distant sea; morning dew burning off into full sunlight

set_pieces.name: Arrival on the chilly shore
set_pieces.what_happens: The motorcycle comes down out of the hills to the chapel shore; wide view of distant seas and the wooded hills behind.
lines: Even here is chilly in the morning.
covers the seas in the distance
hugs the bases of tree-covered hills
set_pieces.camera: extreme wide from the water looking inland, bike small against the hills; slow push
set_pieces.position: shore road dropping to the waterline beside the chapel ruins

set_pieces.name: Remnants in the sunlight
set_pieces.what_happens: Sun crosses the debris of the storm-wrecked chapel and the shattered tambourine from poem 3 (callback).
lines: All the remnants of the destruction revealed in the sunlight.
set_pieces.camera: low macro dolly across debris as light rakes across it; sun flare
set_pieces.position: the chapel remnants on the sand

set_pieces.name: The temple builds itself
set_pieces.what_happens: The POET starts to rebuild; the white futuristic temple rises in unison with his movements.
set_pieces.camera: locked-off time-lapse wide plus a tracking medium on the POET as walls assemble around him
set_pieces.position: the old chapel footprint at the shoreline

set_pieces.name: Choir chords in the new nave (inferred)
set_pieces.what_happens: Inside the clean white hall the old choir stands and prayer lines return remade; sound calms him.
lines: choir chords calm the nerves of things I can't control
offer them as keepsakes back to the higher powers
set_pieces.camera: symmetrical wide down the nave; sunbeam shafts; slow crane up

set_pieces.name: Journal and the lonely mirror (inferred)
set_pieces.what_happens: He opens a journal stored away and reads aloud; a mirror callback to the midnight solitude of earlier poems.
lines: I can close a chapter and open a journal stored away
sung alone as gospels to the lonely mirror's midnight hours
set_pieces.camera: close-up on pages and his profile; over-shoulder into a mirror
set_pieces.position: a quiet side room or alcove of the temple

set_pieces.name: Welcoming the new day
set_pieces.what_happens: Doors open to full sun over the harbor; the finished temple stands bone-white and calm.
lines: We can embrace a new day.
is here together in this sacred place
with this world and a heart at peace.
set_pieces.camera: reverse from inside the doors out to the sea, then wide exterior hero shot of the white temple

arrival.from_previous: End of Magic Ride: he rides out of Atlantis as the sky lightens, through the mountains around Atlantis, and back to the shore at the decaying chapel.

departure.to_next: Ellipsis 'Decades later': the same temple fills with friends and events (the treatment's 'Temple (Cont.)' runs straight into Reunion).

encoding: The temple must rise exactly where the chapel decayed in poem 3: rebuilding on the ruin turns loss into a 'sacred place' rather than escaping it. Putting it on a harbor shore at dawn makes it the film's turn from night to day, the hinge between the escape city (Atlantis) and home. The interior beats are inferred, because the treatment left the poem unwritten.
